angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 576,596 km at 149.57 pc = 0.05 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 6.6858 +/- 0.0197 mas (same row, RUWE 1.03): 149.57 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 0.8288 +/- 0.0115 solar radii from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-1775 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract): 576,596 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 0.9218 +/- 0.0143 solar masses from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-1775 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5284 +/- 50 K from MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1775 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: MacDougall et al. 2023, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-1775 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)

luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1775 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units -0.31605, from MacDougall et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of TOI-1775 (pscomppars): age 0.8 Gyr, from MacDougall et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023AJ....166...33M/abstract)
